body:
Why: strategy agents write task titles that read like summaries of the body. Examples: "Review follow-ups go to the feature's Tech Debt task, and workers are told about it", and "Atomic cross-project extract: a crash finishes or rolls back, never half-applies". A title should capture the essence of the work, what it's for, so it reads well on a board card and in `strategy list`. The specifics belong in the body.

Add guidance to the strategy run's role (`board.rs` `STRATEGY_ROLE`, Spec 15 §6 brief) for proposing tasks, features and milestones:
- A title names what's to be done, in a few words (roughly 3–7). Use the feature's short name as a prefix when that helps (`extract: JS FFI files`).
- No mechanism, conditions, error codes or lists in the title. Those go in the body.
- Keep it short: the brief has a size budget, so one or two sentences.

Also check the agent reference and `help` (`strategy task …`) and mirror the guidance there in one line, if it fits.

**Tests:** the existing strategy brief test (or a new one) asserts that the guidance is present.

**Checks:** `rust-unit`, `rust-acceptance`.
title: Strategy runs: guidance on task titles
